Welcome to The Sheiling Ringwood
Set in a stunning, sustainable and eco-friendly 45-acre site close to the New Forest and Dorset coastline, the natural surroundings of our school and college provide a rich, enabling and therapeutic learning environment for students, aged 5-25, who have a special educational need.
We specialise in autism and communication difficulties, severe and complex learning disabilities and behaviours that challenge.
Our mission is to create an educational, therapeutic community and environment, which upholds each person's human integrity and spiritual wholeness and where every child and young person, both because of and despite their individual challenges, has something to give and something to learn through all of their relationships with others.
Corine van BarneveldPrincipal

Latest Newsletter
The Sheiling Ringwood
Celebrating 75 Years
This year, The Sheiling Ringwood celebrates 75 years of educating and caring for children and young people with special educational needs and this is a milestone we are incredibly proud of. We have spent more than seven decades providing specialist education, residential care and tailored therapy in a calm and nurturing environment. Our school and college are built around strong relationships, consistency, community and truly understanding every young person as an individual who has true potential. Corine van Barneveld, Principal of The Sheiling Ringwood, says this anniversary is a chance to reflect on a rich and diverse history and the ethos and values that have shaped the organisation since its beginnings. “For 75 years, the Sheiling has been guided by the belief that every young person deserves to be known, valued and supported in a way that reflects who they are. That commitment continues to this day and underpins everything we do.”

Sheiling Parents
The idea of the forum is for parents/carers to meet in person (and previously via Microsoft Teams) to converse, share ideas or to just listen in a non-judgemental environment. We all have different thoughts and feelings on a wide range of subjects with the common factor being our children/young people.
We are a unique group of people who can help each other navigate looking after our young people, share ideas, learn about various subjects and have great conversations with other parents/carers who actually do understand-or at least understand more than others might. A bonus is the various members of staff that attend the meetings; an ideal opportunity to pick their brains and learn about their specialist subject!
The forum has continued to evolve since it first started in 2020. In general, a meeting starts with the previous meeting minutes being 'signed off' by a couple of thumbs-up, followed by an informative and interesting update from the different areas of the school and college.
The 'spotlight' feature changes at each meeting: we have covered Fundraising, EHCPs (which turned into individual EHCP events) and the Mental Capacity Act to name a few. Any ideas for future development of the forum are welcome.
The meeting is very relaxed and questions can be raised at any time and these often lead to further questions or start interesting conversations. Also, if you would rather come along just to listen, you are more than welcome. If there is a subject that you are interested in, the Parent Forum team would be happy to include these in future meetings or feedback on an individual basis. The spotlight presentations are often shared (as are the meeting minutes) so you can listen without trying to take detailed notes.
The first in-person meeting was a huge success, lots of attendees chatting, meeting for the first time or meeting in person for the first time, sharing ideas, whole group and smaller group conversations in a relaxed environment with the added bonus of tasty treats.
If you would like to attend the next meeting or would like further information, please contact

Celebrating 75 Years
This year, The Sheiling Ringwood celebrates 75 years of educating and caring for children and young people with special educational needs and this is a milestone we are incredibly proud of.
We have spent more than seven decades providing specialist education, residential care and tailored therapy in a calm and nurturing environment. Our school and college are built around strong relationships, consistency, community and truly understanding every young person as an individual who has true potential.
Corine van Barneveld, Principal of The Sheiling Ringwood, says this anniversary is a chance to reflect on a rich and diverse history and the ethos and values that have shaped the organisation since its beginnings.
“For 75 years, the Sheiling has been guided by the belief that every young person deserves to be known, valued and supported in a way that reflects who they are. That commitment continues to this day and underpins everything we do.”
Our approach has been consistently recognised by Ofsted including in recent inspections where we were praised for the positive relationships between staff and students, the dedication of our teams and the calm, structured environment that helps students feel safe and supported across education and care, providing opportunities for 24/7 learning.
Although we are proud to celebrate our history, we continue to look forward. Recent developments reflect ongoing investment and progress, including the opening of two new purpose‑built school classrooms last year. This September, we will also open a new specialist double classroom for college, enhancing provision for older students and supporting life skills, independence and transition into adulthood.
As Corine adds: “Our focus remains clear - to enable young people with complex needs to live, learn and grow with confidence and opportunity.”
Our 75th anniversary will be marked by a number of different events throughout this year, recognising our journey since 1951 while also looking ahead to the future, culminating in our annual Summer Festival on Saturday 20th June, from 11:30am to 4:00pm. The festival will welcome students, staff and co-workers past and present, their friends and families and will also be open to the public who are always very supportive of this event. The festival will feature live music throughout the day, fabulous food, attractions, games and stalls. Entry is by donation, onsite parking is included and the day promises to be our biggest Summer Festival yet where we will be raising funds for student gym equipment.
